syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Exploring Society India and Beyond
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a map is a top-view drawing of an area, small or large.
Distinguish physical, political and thematic maps and define an atlas.

topics.title: Distance and the scale of a map

concepts.learning_objective: State what a map's scale tells us about map and ground distances.
Calculate real distances from map measurements using a given scale.

topics.title: Direction and symbols on maps
topics.ncert_sections: A Map and Its Components (direction, symbols)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the cardinal and intermediate directions and use them on a map.
Explain why maps use standard symbols and who fixes them for India.

topics.title: Mapping the Earth: the globe and coordinates
topics.ncert_sections: Mapping the Earth; a) Understanding coordinates

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a globe represents the nearly spherical Earth better than a flat map.
Explain how two coordinates together fix a location precisely.
Describe parallels of latitude, the Equator and the poles and their values.
Relate latitude to torrid, temperate and frigid climates.
Describe meridians of longitude and how longitude is measured east and west.
Identify the Greenwich Prime Meridian as the 0 degree reference for longitude.
Describe the ancient Indian prime meridian through Ujjayini.
Relate the Earth's rotation of 15 degrees per hour to local time.
Calculate differences in local time from differences in longitude.

topics.title: Standard time, time zones and the International Date Line

concepts.learning_objective: Explain standard time and Indian Standard Time relative to GMT.
Explain why time zones follow borders and why large countries have several.
Explain the International Date Line and the change of date on crossing it.

topics.title: The Blue Planet: Water and Land on the Earth

concepts.learning_objective: Recall that almost three-fourths of the Earth's surface is water and a little over one-fourth is land, which is why the Earth looks blue from space.
Define oceans and continents and state that both shape the climate and all life on Earth.

topics.title: The Distribution of Water and Land
topics.ncert_sections: The Distribution of Water and Land on the Earth

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that land and water are not equally distributed and that the Northern Hemisphere has more land than the Southern.
Identify parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude on maps of the Earth seen from above the poles.
Distinguish salty seawater from the small share of freshwater found in glaciers, rivers, lakes, the atmosphere and underground.
Name the five oceans and arrange them in order of size.
Explain that the oceans are interconnected and support a rich diversity of marine flora and fauna.
Describe the limits of the Indian Ocean and locate the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal on either side of India.
Explain that oceans bring life-giving monsoon rains but also give rise to destructive storms such as cyclones.
Describe what a tsunami is, what causes it and how it affected India in 2004.
Explain how early warning systems and disaster management help protect lives and property.
Explain why continents can be counted as four, five, six or seven, and identify the most widely used count.
Compare the relative sizes of the seven continents and identify the largest and the smallest.
Define an island and explain why continents, though surrounded by water, are not called islands.
Locate India's two major island groups in the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea.
Describe the Indian Antarctica Programme and its first base station, Dakshin Gangotri.
Explain how oceans bring rain through the water cycle and produce more than half of the world's oxygen.
Describe how people have used oceans for migration, trade, military campaigns, food and culture.
Identify human threats to oceans such as plastic pollution and overfishing and the need to protect them.
Define a landform and describe how landforms are connected with the environment and life.
Identify mountains, plateaus and plains as the three major landforms and recognise them on a real journey.
Describe the features of mountains and distinguish them from hills.
Name major mountain ranges and peaks of the world and of India mentioned in the chapter.
Explain the difference between young and old mountains using the Himalayas and the Aravallis.

topics.title: Mountain environment and life in the mountains
topics.ncert_sections: Mountain environment; Life in the mountains

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the vegetation and animals of mountain environments.
Explain how people farm and earn a living in mountain regions.
Identify natural and human-made challenges of mountain life and the need for balance in tourism.
Describe the features of plateaus and give examples such as the Tibetan and Deccan plateaus.
Explain why plateaus are called storehouses of minerals and how their soils affect farming.

topics.title: Plains and life in the plains

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how floodplains are formed by river sediments and why they are fertile.
Describe occupations in the Ganga plain and evaluate the challenges of irrigation and groundwater use.
Explain the cultural value of rivers, their sources and confluences.

topics.title: Deserts, the tinais and human adaptability

concepts.learning_objective: Describe hot and cold deserts and how humans have adapted to them.
Relate the five tinais of Sangam poetry to their landscapes and main occupations.

topics.title: How Do We Learn About the Past?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what history is and how human history fits within the Earth's very long history.
Identify what geologists, palaeontologists, anthropologists and archaeologists study.

topics.title: How Is Time Measured in History?

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Gregorian calendar, its leap-year rule and the meaning of CE and BCE.
Calculate the number of years between BCE and CE dates, keeping in mind that there is no year zero.

topics.title: Timelines, Centuries, Millenniums and Indian Calendars

concepts.learning_objective: Use a timeline to arrange dates and events in chronological order.
Work out which century or millennium, CE or BCE, a given year belongs to.
State what a panchanga is and what information it provides.

topics.title: What Are the Sources of History?

concepts.learning_objective: Define a source of history and recognise different kinds of sources.
Explain why historians compare many sources and decide which to trust when they disagree.
Identify the experts and scientific studies that help reconstruct the past.
Describe how early humans lived as hunters and gatherers in bands.
Explain what rock paintings, tools and ornaments tell us about early humans.

topics.title: The First Crops and Growing Communities

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the end of the last Ice Age led to settled farming near rivers.
Trace how farming communities grew into villages and towns with new technologies.
Explain that the region called the Indian Subcontinent has had many names and changing boundaries over thousands of years.
Identify ancient texts, travellers' accounts and inscriptions as the sources of India's names.
Recognise the natural boundaries of the Indian Subcontinent on a physical map.

topics.title: How Indians named India: Sapta Sindhava and the regions of the Mahabharata

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning and extent of the Rig Veda's name 'Sapta Sindhava'.
Match regions listed in the Mahabharata with the present-day areas they roughly correspond to.
Explain the meaning of 'Bharatavarsha' and the origin of the name 'Bharata'.
State the meaning of 'Jambudvipa' and its link with the jamun tree.
Explain how Ashoka's inscription helps date the use of 'Jambudvipa' and what area it covered.

topics.title: Bharata: the Vishnu Purana, a Tamil poem and the Constitution

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the Vishnu Purana defines the country called Bharata.
Interpret the ancient Tamil poem's description of the land's extent.
Recall that the Constitution of India begins with the phrase 'India, that is Bharat'.
Explain how the Persian name 'Hindu' was derived from 'Sindhu' as a geographical term.
Trace how Greek and Chinese names for India came from 'Sindhu'.
Recall the origin of 'Hindustan' and the journey of the Chinese traveller Xuanzang.
Identify the characteristics that mark a society as a civilisation.
Place the beginnings of civilisation in Mesopotamia, Egypt and India in time.
Explain how fertile river plains led villages to grow into towns and cities around 2600 BCE.
Explain why the civilisation has several names and why its inhabitants are called Harappans.

topics.title: The Sarasvati River and Harappan Sites

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Sarasvati River, its present names and its mention in the Rig Veda.
Locate major Harappan cities and sites in their modern states or regions.
Describe the main features of Harappan town-planning, such as streets, fortifications and upper and lower towns.
Explain the structure of the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro and the debate about its purpose.
Describe how Harappan houses, drains and wells reflect care for cleanliness and water.
Explain how the reservoirs of Dholavira harvested and stored water.
Identify the crops and farming tools of the Harappans and the link between villages and cities.
Explain how archaeological evidence reveals what the Harappans ate.
Identify Harappan exports, imports and trade routes, including the Lothal dockyard.
Describe Harappan seals and their likely link with trade.
Describe Harappan crafts such as carnelian beads, shell bangles and bronze.

topics.title: The Lives of the Ancients and the End of the Cities

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret Harappan objects of daily use and cultural or symbolic objects.
Explain the factors agreed upon for the decline of Harappan cities and what survived.
Explain what the Vedas are and how their hymns were preserved orally over many generations.
Describe the Vedic ideas of ritam, the many names of one reality, and the call for unity among people.
Identify the janas of early Vedic society and the clues (raja, sabha, samiti) about how they were governed.
Recognise the variety of professions mentioned in the Vedic texts.
Explain the Upanishadic ideas of brahman and atman and why they lead to the idea that all beings are connected.
Interpret the stories of Shvetaketu, Nachiketa and Gargi and the value they place on asking questions.
Identify Vedanta and Yoga as schools that grew out of the Vedas and formed the foundations of Hinduism.
Narrate the main events in the life of Siddhartha Gautama leading to his enlightenment.
Explain the Buddha's teachings on ignorance, attachment, ahimsa and inner discipline.
Describe the Sangha and the values expressed through the Jataka tales.
Describe the life of Mahavira and the lessons of Jain stories such as that of Rohineya.
Explain the Jain principles of ahimsa, anekantavada and aparigraha.

topics.title: Many Schools, One Trunk
topics.ncert_sections: Spread of teachings; Charvaka; shared concepts

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how monks and nuns spread their teachings and the evidence left in monasteries and rock-cut caves.
Explain the diversity of schools of thought, including the Charvaka school, and why the term 'religion' is considered limiting.
Identify the concepts shared by the Vedic, Buddhist and Jain schools that form the 'trunk' of Indian culture.
Define a tribe and explain folk and tribal traditions as oral traditions of India.
Explain how tribal belief systems regard nature as sacred while also holding a concept of a supreme being.
Analyse the two-way interaction between tribal traditions and Hinduism and its result of mutual enrichment.

chapters.title: Unity in Diversity, or 'Many in the One'

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the range of India's diversity in people, languages, dress, food and customs.
Recall the findings of the Anthropological Survey of India's 'People of India' project.
Explain what is meant by 'unity in diversity' in the Indian context.
Identify the staple grains and common spices used across India.
Explain how common ingredients combined in many ways show unity in diversity.
Explain how the sari reflects both unity and diversity.
Recall the long history of Indian textiles, including the Vaishali relief and chintz.
Recognise Makara Sankranti and its regional names as one harvest festival.
Interpret how similar festivals held about the same time show unity in diversity.
Describe how the Panchatantra spread across languages and lands.
Recall the main stories and themes of the Ramayana and the Mahabharata.
Explain how folk and tribal versions of the epics link communities across India.

topics.title: Diversity as Enrichment
topics.ncert_sections: Quotations; Before we move on; Questions

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the idea of 'the Many in the One' in the chapter's quotations.
Evaluate why Indian culture treats diversity as an enrichment rather than a division.
State that the family is the fundamental and most ancient unit of society.
Distinguish joint families from nuclear families and reason about why families take each form.

topics.title: Family relationship terms in Indian languages

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Indian languages name family relationships more precisely than English and why most have no word for cousin.

topics.title: Roles, responsibilities and values in the family

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that family relationships rest on love, care, cooperation and interdependence, with roles for every member.
Identify the values such as ahimsa, dana, seva and tyaga that children learn in the family.

topics.title: Family values in practice: Shalini and Tenzing

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret how Shalini's family in Kerala shared what it had with relatives in difficulty.
Analyse how members of Tenzing's family in Meghalaya share work, decisions and care.

topics.title: Community: meaning, shared resources and service

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a community and explain how agreed practices on shared resources bring both access and duties.
Explain the halma tradition of the Bhils and other examples of serving the community without expecting a return.

topics.title: Communities in cities and the many kinds of community

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate Kamal Parmar's evening classes in Ahmedabad as an example of community spirit in a city.
Explain how Residents' Welfare Associations make rules and why communities are interdependent.
Recognise that community is a flexible concept covering groups based on jati, religion, region, work or interest.
Explain why rules are needed when many people live together in a society.
Distinguish between governance as a process and government as the system that makes and enforces rules and laws.
Identify the roles of the legislature, the executive and the judiciary.
Explain how separation of powers provides checks and balances among the three organs.
Describe the local, State and Central levels of government and when each acts.
Match the organs, heads and main functions of the Central and State governments.
State the meaning and origin of the word democracy.
Distinguish between representative democracy and direct democracy with examples.
Explain grassroots democracy as the participation of ordinary citizens in decisions that affect them.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy – Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas

topics.title: Why local government? The Panchayati Raj system

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a large and diverse country like India needs government at the local level.
Describe the Panchayat as a village council and a form of self-government that brings governance closer to people.

topics.title: The three-tier structure of Panchayati Raj

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the village, block and district tiers of Panchayati Raj and the names of their bodies.
Recognise the range of local matters that Panchayati Raj institutions look after.
Distinguish the Gram Sabha of adult voters from the Gram Panchayat it elects.
Describe the roles of the Sarpanch, the Panchayat Secretary and the Patwari.
Evaluate how committed Sarpanchs working with villagers can transform their villages.
Explain how Bal Sabhas and Bal Panchayats give children a voice in local matters.
Interpret how actions of a Gram Panchayat can make it child-friendly.
Analyse how the Children's Parliament in rural Rajasthan taught democracy through practice.
Describe the Panchayat Samiti as the link between the Gram Panchayat and the Zila Parishad.
Explain how the Panchayat Samiti coordinates development plans and funds across Gram Panchayats.
Explain the reservation of one-third of seats for women and special rules for disadvantaged sections.
Identify the Arthashastra, its author and the subjects it deals with.
Apply Kautilya's plan of headquarters for groups of villages and compare it with today's tiers.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy – Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas

topics.title: Participatory democracy and the levels of governance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain participatory democracy as citizens actively taking part in governance at every level.
Identify the rural and urban sides of the local level in India's pyramid of governance.

topics.title: Urban local bodies and ward committees

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what urban local bodies are and why they are called decentralised.
Describe how cities are divided into wards and what ward committees do.

topics.title: Functions and funding of urban local bodies

concepts.learning_objective: List the main functions and services of urban local bodies.
Explain how urban local bodies raise money through taxes, fines and charges.
Recall the origins of the Madras Corporation as India's oldest municipal institution.

topics.title: Types of urban local bodies
topics.ncert_sections: Urban Local Bodies (Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Nagar Panchayat)

concepts.learning_objective: Classify an urban local body as a Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council or Nagar Panchayat by population.

topics.title: Duties of citizens in urban areas
topics.ncert_sections: Urban Local Bodies; Before we move on

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how citizens' care for their area helps local bodies work efficiently.
Apply the idea of responsible citizenship to everyday civic problems.

topics.title: Village and city: comparing local democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the Panchayati Raj system and urban local bodies.
Explain why everyone's voice matters in local democracy, in villages and cities alike.
Identify economic activities as those performed in exchange for money or money's worth.
Explain the meaning of money's worth and of a market where goods and services are exchanged.
Identify non-economic activities as those done out of love, care, gratitude and respect, not for income.
Classify the activities of a person as economic or non-economic depending on whether they involve payment.

topics.title: Types of economic activities and ways of payment

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between a salary and a wage as forms of payment for work.
Explain a fee and payment in kind as other ways in which people are paid for work.
Calculate the value added when something is transformed into another form and sold.
Recognise which activities and professions create money-related value.
Explain seva as selfless service, such as langars, done without expecting anything in return.
Describe how community efforts like Swachh Bharat Abhiyan and Van Mahotsav add value to society.

topics.title: Economic activities and economic sectors
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; The Classification of Economic Activities into Economic Sectors

concepts.learning_objective: Identify economic activities as those that create monetary value and recognise how their number has grown.
Explain why economic activities with similar characteristics are grouped into primary, secondary and tertiary sectors.
Describe primary activities as those that depend directly on nature to produce goods.
Identify agriculture, mining, fishing, raising livestock and forestry as primary activities.
Explain how secondary activities process outputs of the primary sector into goods for sale or use.
Recognise construction and the supply of water, electricity and gas as part of the secondary sector.
Describe tertiary activities as services that support the primary and secondary sectors and people.
Identify transport, trade, banking, healthcare, teaching and repair as service sector activities.

topics.title: Interdependence among sectors: the AMUL dairy cooperative
topics.ncert_sections: Interdependence Among Sectors; Dairy cooperative: from farm to plate

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the AMUL cooperative freed milk producers from dependence on middlemen.
Trace how milk moves through primary, secondary and tertiary activities in the dairy cooperative.

topics.title: From tree to textbook and recycling paper

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the stages from tree pulp to a printed textbook and link each stage to a sector.
Explain the resources saved by recycling paper and ways to use paper judiciously.
